title: Pane Frattau
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Sardinia's clever way of softening its famously crisp pane carasau, layering it with tomato sauce, pecorino, and a poached egg for a rustic, satisfying dish once favored by shepherds.
longDesc: This dish transforms the shepherd's long-keeping pane carasau, which needs moistening before eating on its own, into a genuinely satisfying meal by soaking the sheets in hot broth and layering them with tomato sauce, cheese, and a soft poached egg.
ingredients: 600 ml (2½ cups) hot vegetable or meat broth
60 ml (¼ cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Warm the olive oil in a saucepan and sauté the garlic briefly, then add the passata and basil, simmering for 15 minutes to make a simple sauce.
Briefly dip a sheet of pane carasau into the hot broth to soften, just a few seconds per side, then place in a wide shallow dish.
Spread a layer of tomato sauce over the softened bread and scatter with grated pecorino.
Repeat with additional softened sheets, sauce, and cheese, building 2–3 layers per portion.
Poach the eggs separately in gently simmering water until the whites are set but yolks remain soft.
Top each portion with a poached egg and an extra scattering of pecorino.
chefTips: Dip the bread only briefly in the hot broth — too long and it will disintegrate rather than simply soften.
Build individual portions rather than one large dish, as the layered bread can become fragile once softened.
A well-made, runny poached egg is essential, as its yolk becomes part of the sauce when broken.
commonMistakes: Oversoaking the bread, causing it to fall apart rather than softening into pliable layers.
Overcooking the eggs, losing the runny yolk that's meant to mix into the dish.
Skimping on the pecorino, which is a defining flavor element.
storage: Best eaten immediately; the softened bread does not hold well.
reheating: Not recommended; best assembled and eaten fresh.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the egg and cheese, with lycopene from the tomato sauce.
culturalNote: Pane frattau was historically a practical shepherd's meal, transforming the long-lasting pane carasau bread into a hearty dish using whatever tomato sauce, cheese, and eggs were on hand.
